reflection.text:
Post-unblinding reflection - predicted DNA replication (p=0.71), truth Protein degradation / lactacystin. This is a primary research screening interpretation, not clinical advice.

What the run got right:
The high-dose imaging signal was strong and internally consistent. At w_fd3018771c 10uM (371 cells) we saw cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+9.3, nuc_dna_mean z=-8.4, cell_major_axis +7.4; replicated at 1uM (+4.2/+3.4/+3.2, 244 cells) and 3uM (+5.7/-5.2/+4.3, 213 cells) with monotonic dose-response rho=+1.00 for cell_nuc_area_ratio and cell_area and rho=-1.00 for nuc_dna_mean, nuc_dna_integrated and cell_count across 3-4 doses. That, plus describe_phenotype 'density lower vs DMSO' and frac_mitotic_like rho=-1.00 and nuc_area rho=0.50 p=0.67, correctly argued against Aurora (no enlarged nuclei), Eg5 (no monopolar mitotic increase) and microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer or actin disruptor (tub_mean rho=+1.00, microscopist 'tubulin/actin intact'). The reviewer summary captured this: flat/down mitotic fraction and intact cytoskeletons.

What misled us and why:
1. Phenocopy: Dose-proportional DNA loss + cell enlargement + cytostasis was read as primary replication block. Lactacystin is a prototypical proteasome inhibitor PMID 11082705. Proteasome inhibition causes accumulation of CDKIs / cyclins, p53, and G1/S arrest with hypertrophy and proliferation block, which produces the same population-average decrease in DNA mean/integrated intensity (fewer S/G2 cells) and increased cell_area / cell_nuc_area_ratio without increased nuc_area. We anchored on nuc_dna_mean z=-8.4 and rho=-1.00 as replication stress (e7,e8,e9,e10) and did not consider proteostatic arrest as an alternative cause of S-depletion. Our second literature search 'proteasome inhibitor cell size enlargement cell cycle arrest phenotype' returned 0 hits and failed to close that gap.

2. Atlas bias: compare_to_reference_atlas e6 nearest neighbours were DNA replication 5/10, Kinase inhibitors 4/10, Microtubule destabilizers 1/10. We used that to update_hypotheses e16 to DNA replication 0.70, DNA damage 0.14, Kinase 0.08, Protein degradation 0.02 with contradicting evidence [e6]. The atlas under-represented proteasome inhibitors - e18/e19 lookup_compound returned CHEMBL374308 / CID6610292 with 'mechanisms: none curated' pre-unblinding, so there was no proteasome reference to compete. We treated atlas similarity as mechanistic support rather than library coverage.

3. Acquisition/statistical overconfidence: We sampled only 3-4 wells each n=1 (0.1, 1, 3, 10 uM) with 213-423 cells/well. With n=3 for dose_response, Spearman rho= +/-1.00 gives p=0 by calculation but is not robust inference; we treated it as confirmatory. The consistent trend across the 3uM fill-in (e15) reinforced DNA replication and we stopped at budget 0 without a proteasome-orthogonal readout. Hypotheses e16 explicitly listed Protein degradation supporting e2 but contradicting e6 - we dismissed it on atlas grounds.

4. Feature-level ambiguity: tub_std z=-2.8 at 0.1uM (e4) briefly suggested destabilizer, but dose_response tub_mean rho=+1.00 correctly excluded it; we then over-read 'intact microtubules = not proteasome.' No ubiquitin, aggresome, or proteasome activity reporter was acquired; describe_phenotype e5 returned 'candidates: unknown' on 4 fields - insufficient to discriminate proteasome from replication arrest visually.

Lesson: When a reversible cytostatic + hypertrophic + low-DNA signal is strongly dose-proportional and atlas-favored, we should explicitly test proteostasis vs replication by orthogonal assays - e.g., poly-ubiquitin accumulation, proteasome activity probe, and EdU/BrdU S-phase fraction with PI cell-cycle distribution - and down-weight atlas when known classes are missing from the reference set. That would have distinguished G1-arrested proteasome block from primary DNA synthesis inhibition.
reflection.next_experiment: High-content poly-ubiquitin/K48 IF + proteasome activity probe plus EdU/PI flow across 0.1-10 uM alongside bortezomib reference to separate proteasome-dependent G1 arrest/hypertrophy from primary replication inhibition.
